nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma = \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, viewed inside $G = \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, and let $u_t = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ t & 1 \end{pmatrix}$. For every $x \in G$, the orbit $\{\Gamma x u_t : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ of the horocycle flow on the space $\Gamma \backslash G$ of right cosets, with the quotient topology, is either closed or dense.
nodes.title: Orbits of the horocycle flow on SL(2, ℤ) \ SL(2, ℝ) are closed or dense

nodes.summary: The horocycle one-parameter subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ is $u_t = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ t & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$; it satisfies $u_{s+t} = u_s u_t$ and every $u_t$ is unipotent. On $\Gamma \backslash \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ the flow $\Gamma x \mapsto \Gamma x u_t$ is the horocycle flow.
nodes.title: Horocycle one-parameter subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $Q$ be a real quadratic form in $n \ge 3$ variables. Suppose that $Q$ is indefinite (it takes a positive and a negative value), nondegenerate (no nonzero $x$ satisfies $Q(v + x) = Q(v - x)$ for all $v$) and not a scalar multiple of a form with integer coefficients, that is, not of the form $x \mapsto c \sum_{i,j} a_{ij} x_i x_j$ with $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a_{ij} \in \mathbb{Z}$. nodes.title: Margulis's theorem on values of quadratic forms (Oppenheim conjecture)

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.
